decision: voided by the team (operator decision, 31 Oct 2026); disclosed in CLAUDE.md
what_happened: While hand-checking the Step 3 agent tools, a notebook cell meant to show finalize() refusing a failed run was given the killed tool-check run m-eurosat-0005 instead (the intended out-of-memory run was rejected at launch and the notebook picked the most recent run id). finalize accepted killed runs, so the m-eurosat test split was evaluated once.
impact: Test accuracy 0.895 of a throwaway 5-epoch ResNet18 was observed. No model, config or decision was chosen using it. m-eurosat will be finalized once more, with a model selected on validation only; that later test score must be reported together with this incident.
fixes: tool checks run in a sandbox workspace (GOTRAIN_WORKSPACE) where finalize/final_test refuse
check notebook takes run ids from launch results and stops on unexpected results

decision: not voided: m-SA-crop-type is reported without a test score (operator decision, 1 Nov 2026 ~00:35Z). Its with/without-playbook result uses the validation split only (PROTOCOL.md) and is unaffected.
what_happened: The chain's finalize for m-SA-crop-type (session m-SA-crop-type__main__chain; incumbent = Level 2 composite m-SA-crop-type-L2-006) was killed by the kernel's out-of-memory killer at 00:28Z while final_test loaded the test split into memory (float32 path: ~3.4 GB array plus copies for channel selection and the 8-bit rescale, ~9 GB peak on a 15 GB instance). The machine-wide test registry had already recorded 'opened' at 00:26:49Z, which by design is written before the test split is read.
impact: No prediction, metric or test_stats.npz was produced: there is no vault entry and the agent's finalize call returned nothing. The test split was read from disk into the gitignored cache file workspace/cache/m-SA-crop-type/test.npz. By the registry rule an 'opened' line without 'done' consumes the task's one test touch, so final_test refuses m-SA-crop-type: the guard held.
fixes: none applied to the frozen chain code
post-hackathon: a memory-lean test loader (batches streamed from the HDF5 split or a memory-mapped test cache)
